We say that $f$ is of {\it finite type at $x \in X$} if there exists an affine open neighbourhood $\Spec(A) = U \subset X$ of $x$ and an affine open $\Spec(R) = V \subset S$ with $f(U) \subset V$ such that the induced ring map $R \to A$ is of finite type. We say that $f$ is {\it locally of finite type} if it is of finite type at every point of $X$. We say that $f$ is of {\it finite type} if it is locally of finite type and quasi-compact.

label: lemma-locally-finite-type-characterize
statement: Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes. The following are equivalent The morphism $f$ is locally of finite type. For all affine opens $U \subset X$, $V \subset S$ with $f(U) \subset V$ the ring map $\mathcal{O}_S(V) \to \mathcal{O}_X(U)$ is of finite type. There exist an open covering $S = \bigcup_{j \in J} V_j$ and open coverings $f^{-1}(V_j) = \bigcup_{i \in I_j} U_i$ such that each of the morphisms $U_i \to V_j$, $j\in J, i\in I_j$ is locally of finite type. There exist an affine open covering $S = \bigcup_{j \in J} V_j$ and affine open coverings $f^{-1}(V_j) = \bigcup_{i \in I_j} U_i$ such that the ring map $\mathcal{O}_S(V_j) \to \mathcal{O}_X(U_i)$ is of finite type, for all $j\in J, i\in I_j$. Moreover, if $f$ is locally of finite type then for any open subschemes $U \subset X$, $V \subset S$ with $f(U) \subset V$ the restriction $f|_U : U \to V$ is locally of finite type.

label: lemma-composition-finite-type
statement: The composition of two morphisms which are locally of finite type is locally of finite type. The same is true for morphisms of finite type.

label: lemma-base-change-finite-type
statement: The base change of a morphism which is locally of finite type is locally of finite type. The same is true for morphisms of finite type.

label: lemma-immersion-locally-finite-type
statement: A closed immersion is of finite type. An immersion is locally of finite type.

label: lemma-finite-type-noetherian
statement: Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism. If $S$ is (locally) Noetherian and $f$ (locally) of finite type then $X$ is (locally) Noetherian.

label: lemma-finite-type-Noetherian-quasi-separated
statement: Let $f : X \to S$ be locally of finite type with $S$ locally Noetherian. Then $f$ is quasi-separated.

label: lemma-permanence-finite-type
statement: Let $X \to Y$ be a morphism of schemes over a base scheme $S$. If $X$ is locally of finite type over $S$, then $X \to Y$ is locally of finite type.

label: lemma-point-finite-type
section: Points of finite type and Jacobson schemes
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $k$ be a field. Let $f : \Spec(k) \to S$ be a morphism. The following are equivalent: The morphism $f$ is of finite type. The morphism $f$ is locally of finite type. There exists an affine open $U = \Spec(R)$ of $S$ such that $f$ corresponds to a finite ring map $R \to k$. There exists an affine open $U = \Spec(R)$ of $S$ such that the image of $f$ consists of a closed point $u$ in $U$ and the field extension $k/\kappa(u)$ is finite.

label: lemma-artinian-finite-type
section: Points of finite type and Jacobson schemes
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $A$ be an Artinian local ring with residue field $\kappa$. Let $f : \Spec(A) \to S$ be a morphism of schemes. Then $f$ is of finite type if and only if the composition $\Spec(\kappa) \to \Spec(A) \to S$ is of finite type.

label: definition-finite-type-point
section: Points of finite type and Jacobson schemes
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme. Let us say that a point $s$ of $S$ is a {\it finite type point} if the canonical morphism $\Spec(\kappa(s)) \to S$ is of finite type. We denote $S_{\text{ft-pts}}$ the set of finite type points of $S$.

label: lemma-identify-finite-type-points
section: Points of finite type and Jacobson schemes
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme. We have $$ S_{\text{ft-pts}} = \bigcup\nolimits_{U \subset S\text{ open}} U_0 $$ where $U_0$ is the set of closed points of $U$. Here we may let $U$ range over all opens or over all affine opens of $S$.

label: lemma-finite-type-points-morphism
section: Points of finite type and Jacobson schemes
statement: Let $f : T \to S$ be a morphism of schemes. If $f$ is locally of finite type, then $f(T_{\text{ft-pts}}) \subset S_{\text{ft-pts}}$.

label: lemma-finite-type-points-surjective-morphism
section: Points of finite type and Jacobson schemes
statement: Let $f : T \to S$ be a morphism of schemes. If $f$ is locally of finite type and surjective, then $f(T_{\text{ft-pts}}) = S_{\text{ft-pts}}$.

label: lemma-enough-finite-type-points
section: Points of finite type and Jacobson schemes
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme. For any locally closed subset $T \subset S$ we have $$ T \not = \emptyset \Rightarrow T \cap S_{\text{ft-pts}} \not = \emptyset. $$ In particular, for any closed subset $T \subset S$ we see that $T \cap S_{\text{ft-pts}}$ is dense in $T$.

label: lemma-jacobson-finite-type-points
section: Points of finite type and Jacobson schemes
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme. The following are equivalent: the scheme $S$ is Jacobson, $S_{\text{ft-pts}}$ is the set of closed points of $S$, for all $T \to S$ locally of finite type closed points map to closed points, and for all $T \to S$ locally of finite type closed points $t \in T$ map to closed points $s \in S$ with $\kappa(s) \subset \kappa(t)$ finite.

label: lemma-Jacobson-universally-Jacobson
section: Points of finite type and Jacobson schemes
statement: Let $S$ be a Jacobson scheme. Any scheme locally of finite type over $S$ is Jacobson.

label: lemma-ubiquity-Jacobson-schemes
section: Points of finite type and Jacobson schemes
statement: The following types of schemes are Jacobson. Any scheme locally of finite type over a field. Any scheme locally of finite type over $\mathbf{Z}$. Any scheme locally of finite type over a $1$-dimensional Noetherian domain with infinitely many primes. A scheme of the form $\Spec(R) \setminus \{\mathfrak m\}$ where $(R, \mathfrak m)$ is a Noetherian local ring. Also any scheme locally of finite type over it.

label: definition-universally-catenary
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme. Assume $S$ is locally Noetherian. We say $S$ is {\it universally catenary} if for every morphism $X \to S$ locally of finite type the scheme $X$ is catenary.

label: lemma-universally-catenary-local
statement: Let $S$ be a locally Noetherian scheme. The following are equivalent $S$ is universally catenary, there exists an open covering of $S$ all of whose members are universally catenary schemes, for every affine open $\Spec(R) = U \subset S$ the ring $R$ is universally catenary, and there exists an affine open covering $S = \bigcup U_i$ such that each $U_i$ is the spectrum of a universally catenary ring. Moreover, in this case any scheme locally of finite type over $S$ is universally catenary as well.

label: lemma-universally-catenary-local-rings-universally-catenary
statement: Let $S$ be a locally Noetherian scheme. The following are equivalent: $S$ is universally catenary, and all local rings $\mathcal{O}_{S, s}$ of $S$ are universally catenary.

label: lemma-catenary-check-irreducible
statement: Let $S$ be a locally Noetherian scheme. Then $S$ is universally catenary if and only if the irreducible components of $S$ are universally catenary.

label: lemma-ubiquity-uc
statement: The following types of schemes are universally catenary. Any scheme locally of finite type over a field. Any scheme locally of finite type over a Cohen-Macaulay scheme. Any scheme locally of finite type over $\mathbf{Z}$. Any scheme locally of finite type over a $1$-dimensional Noetherian domain. And so on.

label: lemma-finite-type-nagata
statement: Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism. If $S$ is Nagata and $f$ locally of finite type then $X$ is Nagata. If $S$ is universally Japanese and $f$ locally of finite type then $X$ is universally Japanese.

label: lemma-ubiquity-nagata
statement: The following types of schemes are Nagata. Any scheme locally of finite type over a field. Any scheme locally of finite type over a Noetherian complete local ring. Any scheme locally of finite type over $\mathbf{Z}$. Any scheme locally of finite type over a Dedekind ring of characteristic zero. And so on.

label: definition-J
statement: Let $X$ be a locally Noetherian scheme. We say $X$ is {\it J-2} if for every morphism $Y \to X$ which is locally of finite type the regular locus $\text{Reg}(Y)$ is open in $Y$.

label: lemma-J
statement: Let $X$ be a locally Noetherian scheme. The following are equivalent $X$ is J-2, there exists an open covering of $X$ all of whose members are J-2 schemes, for every affine open $\Spec(R) = U \subset X$ the ring $R$ is J-2, and there exists an affine open covering $S = \bigcup U_i$ such that each $\mathcal{O}(U_i)$ is J-2 for all $i$. Moreover, in this case any scheme locally of finite type over $X$ is J-2 as well.

label: lemma-ubiquity-J-2
statement: The following types of schemes are J-2. Any scheme locally of finite type over a field. Any scheme locally of finite type over a Noetherian complete local ring. Any scheme locally of finite type over $\mathbf{Z}$. Any scheme locally of finite type over a Noetherian local ring of dimension $1$. Any scheme locally of finite type over a Nagata ring of dimension $1$. Any scheme locally of finite type over a Dedekind ring of characteristic zero. And so on.

label: definition-excellent
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme. We say $X$ is {\it quasi-excellent} if for every $x \in X$ there exists an affine open neighbourhood $x \in U \subset X$ such that the ring $\mathcal{O}_X(U)$ is quasi-excellent (see More on Algebra, Definition \ref{more-algebra-definition-excellent}). We say $X$ is {\it excellent} if for every $x \in X$ there exists an affine open neighbourhood $x \in U \subset X$ such that the ring $\mathcal{O}_X(U)$ is excellent (see More on Algebra, Definition \ref{more-algebra-definition-excellent}).

label: lemma-characterize-quasi-excellent
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme. The following are equivalent $X$ is quasi-excellent, and $X$ is a G-scheme and J-2.

label: lemma-quasi-excellent-nagata
statement: A quasi-excellent scheme is Nagata.

label: lemma-characterize-excellent
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme. The following are equivalent $X$ is excellent, and $X$ is quasi-excellent and universally catenary.

label: lemma-locally-excellent
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme. The following are equivalent: The scheme $X$ is (quasi-)excellent. For every affine open $U \subset X$ the ring $\mathcal{O}_X(U)$ is (quasi-)excellent. There exists an affine open covering $X = \bigcup U_i$ such that each $\mathcal{O}_X(U_i)$ is (quasi-)excellent. There exists an open covering $X = \bigcup X_j$ such that each open subscheme $X_j$ is (quasi-)excellent. Moreover, if $X$ is (quasi-)excellent then every open subscheme is (quasi-)excellent.

label: lemma-finite-type-excellent
statement: Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism. If $S$ is (quasi-)excellent and $f$ locally of finite type then $X$ is (quasi-)excellent.

label: lemma-ubiquity-excellent
statement: The following types of schemes are excellent. Any scheme locally of finite type over a field. Any scheme locally of finite type over a Noetherian complete local ring. Any scheme locally of finite type over $\mathbf{Z}$. Any scheme locally of finite type over a Dedekind ring of characteristic zero.

label: definition-quasi-finite
statement: Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes. We say that $f$ is {\it quasi-finite at a point $x \in X$} if there exist an affine neighbourhood $\Spec(A) = U \subset X$ of $x$ and an affine open $\Spec(R) = V \subset S$ such that $f(U) \subset V$, the ring map $R \to A$ is of finite type, and $R \to A$ is quasi-finite at the prime of $A$ corresponding to $x$ (see above). We say $f$ is {\it locally quasi-finite} if $f$ is quasi-finite at every point $x$ of $X$. We say that $f$ is {\it quasi-finite} if $f$ is of finite type and every point $x$ is an isolated point of its fibre.

label: lemma-algebraic-residue-field-extension-closed-point-fibre
statement: Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes. Let $x \in X$ be a point. Set $s = f(x)$. If $\kappa(x)/\kappa(s)$ is an algebraic field extension, then $x$ is a closed point of its fibre, and if in addition $s$ is a closed point of $S$, then $x$ is a closed point of $X$.

label: lemma-closed-point-fibre-locally-finite-type
statement: Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes. Let $x \in X$ be a point. Set $s = f(x)$. Assume $f$ is locally of finite type. Then $x$ is a closed point of its fibre if and only if $\kappa(x)/\kappa(s)$ is a finite field extension.

label: lemma-base-change-closed-point-fibre-locally-finite-type
statement: Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes which is locally of finite type. Let $g : S' \to S$ be any morphism. Denote $f' : X' \to S'$ the base change. If $x' \in X'$ maps to a point $x \in X$ which is closed in $X_{f(x)}$ then $x'$ is closed in $X'_{f'(x')}$.

label: lemma-residue-field-quasi-finite
statement: Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes. Let $x \in X$ be a point. Set $s = f(x)$. If $f$ is quasi-finite at $x$, then the residue field extension $\kappa(x)/\kappa(s)$ is finite.

label: lemma-quasi-finite-at-point-characterize
statement: Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes. Let $x \in X$ be a point. Set $s = f(x)$. Let $X_s$ be the fibre of $f$ at $s$. Assume $f$ is locally of finite type. The following are equivalent: The morphism $f$ is quasi-finite at $x$. The point $x$ is isolated in $X_s$. The point $x$ is closed in $X_s$ and there is no point $x' \in X_s$, $x' \not = x$ which specializes to $x$. For any pair of affine opens $\Spec(A) = U \subset X$, $\Spec(R) = V \subset S$ with $f(U) \subset V$ and $x \in U$ corresponding to $\mathfrak q \subset A$ the ring map $R \to A$ is quasi-finite at $\mathfrak q$.

label: lemma-finite-fibre
statement: Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes. Let $s \in S$. Assume that $f$ is locally of finite type, and $f^{-1}(\{s\})$ is a finite set. Then $X_s$ is a finite discrete topological space, and $f$ is quasi-finite at each point of $X$ lying over $s$.

label: lemma-locally-quasi-finite-fibres
slogan: Finite type morphisms with discrete fibers are quasi-finite.
statement: Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes. Assume $f$ is locally of finite type. Then the following are equivalent $f$ is locally quasi-finite, for every $s \in S$ the fibre $X_s$ is a discrete topological space, and for every morphism $\Spec(k) \to S$ where $k$ is a field the base change $X_k$ has an underlying discrete topological space.

label: lemma-quasi-finite-locally-quasi-compact
statement: Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes. Then $f$ is quasi-finite if and only if $f$ is locally quasi-finite and quasi-compact.

label: lemma-quasi-finite
statement: Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes. The following are equivalent: $f$ is quasi-finite, and $f$ is locally of finite type, quasi-compact, and has finite fibres.

label: lemma-locally-quasi-finite-characterize
statement: Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes. The following are equivalent The morphism $f$ is locally quasi-finite. For every pair of affine opens $U \subset X$, $V \subset S$ with $f(U) \subset V$ the ring map $\mathcal{O}_S(V) \to \mathcal{O}_X(U)$ is quasi-finite. There exists an open covering $S = \bigcup_{j \in J} V_j$ and open coverings $f^{-1}(V_j) = \bigcup_{i \in I_j} U_i$ such that each of the morphisms $U_i \to V_j$, $j\in J, i\in I_j$ is locally quasi-finite. There exists an affine open covering $S = \bigcup_{j \in J} V_j$ and affine open coverings $f^{-1}(V_j) = \bigcup_{i \in I_j} U_i$ such that the ring map $\mathcal{O}_S(V_j) \to \mathcal{O}_X(U_i)$ is quasi-finite, for all $j\in J, i\in I_j$. Moreover, if $f$ is locally quasi-finite then for any open subschemes $U \subset X$, $V \subset S$ with $f(U) \subset V$ the restriction $f|_U : U \to V$ is locally quasi-finite.

label: lemma-composition-quasi-finite
statement: The composition of two morphisms which are locally quasi-finite is locally quasi-finite. The same is true for quasi-finite morphisms.

label: lemma-base-change-quasi-finite
slogan: (Locally) quasi-finite morphisms are stable under base change.
statement: Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes. Let $g : S' \to S$ be a morphism of schemes. Denote $f' : X' \to S'$ the base change of $f$ by $g$ and denote $g' : X' \to X$ the projection. Assume $X$ is locally of finite type over $S$. Let $U \subset X$ (resp.\ $U' \subset X'$) be the set of points where $f$ (resp.\ $f'$) is quasi-finite. Then $U' = U \times_S S' = (g')^{-1}(U)$. The base change of a locally quasi-finite morphism is locally quasi-finite. The base change of a quasi-finite morphism is quasi-finite.

label: lemma-quasi-finite-at-a-finite-number-of-points
statement: Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes of finite type. Let $s \in S$. There are at most finitely many points of $X$ lying over $s$ at which $f$ is quasi-finite.

label: lemma-monomorphism-loc-finite-type-loc-quasi-finite
statement: Let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of schemes. If $f$ is locally of finite type and a monomorphism, then $f$ is separated and locally quasi-finite.

label: lemma-immersion-locally-quasi-finite
statement: Any immersion is locally quasi-finite.

label: lemma-permanence-quasi-finite
statement: Let $X \to Y$ be a morphism of schemes over a base scheme $S$. Let $x \in X$. If $X \to S$ is quasi-finite at $x$, then $X \to Y$ is quasi-finite at $x$. If $X$ is locally quasi-finite over $S$, then $X \to Y$ is locally quasi-finite.

label: lemma-quasi-finite-local-source
statement: Let $f : X \to Y$ and $g : Y \to S$ be morphisms of schemes. If $f$ is surjective, $g \circ f$ locally quasi-finite, and $g$ locally of finite type, then $g : Y \to S$ is locally quasi-finite.

label: definition-finite-presentation
statement: Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes. We say that $f$ is of {\it finite presentation at $x \in X$} if there exists an affine open neighbourhood $\Spec(A) = U \subset X$ of $x$ and affine open $\Spec(R) = V \subset S$ with $f(U) \subset V$ such that the induced ring map $R \to A$ is of finite presentation. We say that $f$ is {\it locally of finite presentation} if it is of finite presentation at every point of $X$. We say that $f$ is of {\it finite presentation} if it is locally of finite presentation, quasi-compact and quasi-separated.

label: lemma-locally-finite-presentation-characterize
statement: Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes. The following are equivalent The morphism $f$ is locally of finite presentation. For every affine opens $U \subset X$, $V \subset S$ with $f(U) \subset V$ the ring map $\mathcal{O}_S(V) \to \mathcal{O}_X(U)$ is of finite presentation. There exist an open covering $S = \bigcup_{j \in J} V_j$ and open coverings $f^{-1}(V_j) = \bigcup_{i \in I_j} U_i$ such that each of the morphisms $U_i \to V_j$, $j\in J, i\in I_j$ is locally of finite presentation. There exist an affine open covering $S = \bigcup_{j \in J} V_j$ and affine open coverings $f^{-1}(V_j) = \bigcup_{i \in I_j} U_i$ such that the ring map $\mathcal{O}_S(V_j) \to \mathcal{O}_X(U_i)$ is of finite presentation, for all $j\in J, i\in I_j$. Moreover, if $f$ is locally of finite presentation then for any open subschemes $U \subset X$, $V \subset S$ with $f(U) \subset V$ the restriction $f|_U : U \to V$ is locally of finite presentation.

label: lemma-composition-finite-presentation
statement: The composition of two morphisms which are locally of finite presentation is locally of finite presentation. The same is true for morphisms of finite presentation.

label: lemma-base-change-finite-presentation
statement: The base change of a morphism which is locally of finite presentation is locally of finite presentation. The same is true for morphisms of finite presentation.

label: lemma-open-immersion-locally-finite-presentation
statement: Any open immersion is locally of finite presentation.

label: lemma-quasi-compact-open-immersion-finite-presentation
statement: Any open immersion is of finite presentation if and only if it is quasi-compact.

label: lemma-closed-immersion-finite-presentation
slogan: Closed immersions of finite presentation correspond to quasi-coherent sheaves of ideals of finite type.
statement: A closed immersion $i : Z \to X$ is of finite presentation if and only if the associated quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals $\mathcal{I} = \Ker(\mathcal{O}_X \to i_*\mathcal{O}_Z)$ is of finite type (as an $\mathcal{O}_X$-module).

label: lemma-finite-presentation-finite-type
statement: A morphism which is locally of finite presentation is locally of finite type. A morphism of finite presentation is of finite type.

label: lemma-noetherian-finite-type-finite-presentation
slogan: Over a locally Noetherian base, finite type is finite presentation.
statement: Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism. If $S$ is locally Noetherian and $f$ locally of finite type then $f$ is locally of finite presentation. If $S$ is locally Noetherian and $f$ of finite type then $f$ is of finite presentation.

label: lemma-finite-presentation-quasi-compact-quasi-separated
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme which is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. If $X$ is of finite presentation over $S$, then $X$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated.

label: lemma-finite-presentation-permanence
statement: Let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of schemes over $S$. If $X$ is locally of finite presentation over $S$ and $Y$ is locally of finite type over $S$, then $f$ is locally of finite presentation. If $X$ is of finite presentation over $S$ and $Y$ is quasi-separated and locally of finite type over $S$, then $f$ is of finite presentation.

label: lemma-diagonal-morphism-finite-type
statement: Let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of schemes with diagonal $\Delta : X \to X \times_Y X$. If $f$ is locally of finite type then $\Delta$ is locally of finite presentation. If $f$ is quasi-separated and locally of finite type, then $\Delta$ is of finite presentation.

label: lemma-inverse-image-constructible
statement: Let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of schemes. Let $E \subset Y$ be a subset. If $E$ is (locally) constructible in $Y$, then $f^{-1}(E)$ is (locally) constructible in $X$.

label: lemma-chevalley
statement: Let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of schemes. Assume $f$ is quasi-compact and locally of finite presentation, and $Y$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Then the image of every constructible subset of $X$ is constructible in $Y$.

label: theorem-chevalley
title: Chevalley's Theorem
statement: Let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of schemes. Assume $f$ is quasi-compact and locally of finite presentation. Then the image of every locally constructible subset is locally constructible.

label: lemma-constructible-containing-open
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme. Let $x \in X$. Let $E \subset X$ be a locally constructible subset. If $\{x' \mid x' \leadsto x\} \subset E$, then $E$ contains an open neighbourhood of $x$.

label: definition-open
statement: Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism. We say $f$ is {\it open} if the map on underlying topological spaces is open. We say $f$ is {\it universally open} if for any morphism of schemes $S' \to S$ the base change $f' : X_{S'} \to S'$ is open.

label: lemma-locally-finite-presentation-universally-open
statement: Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism. If $f$ is locally of finite presentation and generalizations lift along $f$, then $f$ is open. If $f$ is locally of finite presentation and generalizations lift along every base change of $f$, then $f$ is universally open.

label: lemma-composition-open
statement: A composition of (universally) open morphisms is (universally) open.

label: lemma-scheme-over-field-universally-open
statement: Let $k$ be a field. Let $X$ be a scheme over $k$. The structure morphism $X \to \Spec(k)$ is universally open.

label: lemma-open-generizing
statement: Let $\varphi : X \to Y$ be a morphism of schemes. If $\varphi$ is open, then $\varphi$ is generizing (i.e., generalizations lift along $\varphi$). If $\varphi$ is universally open, then $\varphi$ is universally generizing.

label: lemma-descent-quasi-compact
statement: Let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of schemes. Let $g : Y' \to Y$ be open and surjective such that the base change $f' : X' \to Y'$ is quasi-compact. Then $f$ is quasi-compact.

label: definition-submersive
statement: Let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of schemes. We say $f$ is {\it submersive}\footnote{This is very different from the notion of a submersion of differential manifolds.} if the continuous map of underlying topological spaces is submersive, see Topology, Definition \ref{topology-definition-submersive}. We say $f$ is {\it universally submersive} if for every morphism of schemes $Y' \to Y$ the base change $Y' \times_Y X \to Y'$ is submersive.

label: lemma-base-change-universally-submersive
statement: The base change of a universally submersive morphism of schemes by any morphism of schemes is universally submersive.

label: lemma-composition-universally-submersive
statement: The composition of a pair of (universally) submersive morphisms of schemes is (universally) submersive.

label: definition-flat
statement: Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes. Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a quasi-coherent sheaf of $\mathcal{O}_X$-modules. We say $f$ is {\it flat at a point $x \in X$} if the local ring $\mathcal{O}_{X, x}$ is flat over the local ring $\mathcal{O}_{S, f(x)}$. We say that $\mathcal{F}$ is {\it flat over $S$ at a point $x \in X$} if the stalk $\mathcal{F}_x$ is a flat $\mathcal{O}_{S, f(x)}$-module. We say $f$ is {\it flat} if $f$ is flat at every point of $X$. We say that $\mathcal{F}$ is {\it flat over $S$} if $\mathcal{F}$ is flat over $S$ at every point $x$ of $X$.

label: lemma-flat-module-characterize
statement: Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes. Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a quasi-coherent sheaf of $\mathcal{O}_X$-modules. The following are equivalent The sheaf $\mathcal{F}$ is flat over $S$. For every affine opens $U \subset X$, $V \subset S$ with $f(U) \subset V$ the $\mathcal{O}_S(V)$-module $\mathcal{F}(U)$ is flat. There exists an open covering $S = \bigcup_{j \in J} V_j$ and open coverings $f^{-1}(V_j) = \bigcup_{i \in I_j} U_i$ such that each of the modules $\mathcal{F}|_{U_i}$ is flat over $V_j$, for all $j\in J, i\in I_j$. There exists an affine open covering $S = \bigcup_{j \in J} V_j$ and affine open coverings $f^{-1}(V_j) = \bigcup_{i \in I_j} U_i$ such that $\mathcal{F}(U_i)$ is a flat $\mathcal{O}_S(V_j)$-module, for all $j\in J, i\in I_j$. Moreover, if $\mathcal{F}$ is flat over $S$ then for any open subschemes $U \subset X$, $V \subset S$ with $f(U) \subset V$ the restriction $\mathcal{F}|_U$ is flat over $V$.

label: lemma-flat-characterize
statement: Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes. The following are equivalent The morphism $f$ is flat. For every affine opens $U \subset X$, $V \subset S$ with $f(U) \subset V$ the ring map $\mathcal{O}_S(V) \to \mathcal{O}_X(U)$ is flat. There exists an open covering $S = \bigcup_{j \in J} V_j$ and open coverings $f^{-1}(V_j) = \bigcup_{i \in I_j} U_i$ such that each of the morphisms $U_i \to V_j$, $j\in J, i\in I_j$ is flat. There exists an affine open covering $S = \bigcup_{j \in J} V_j$ and affine open coverings $f^{-1}(V_j) = \bigcup_{i \in I_j} U_i$ such that $\mathcal{O}_S(V_j) \to \mathcal{O}_X(U_i)$ is flat, for all $j\in J, i\in I_j$. Moreover, if $f$ is flat then for any open subschemes $U \subset X$, $V \subset S$ with $f(U) \subset V$ the restriction $f|_U : U \to V$ is flat.

label: lemma-pushforward-flat-affine
statement: Let $f : X \to Y$ be an affine morphism of schemes over a base scheme $S$. Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a quasi-coherent $\mathcal{O}_X$-module. Then $\mathcal{F}$ is flat over $S$ if and only if $f_*\mathcal{F}$ is flat over $S$.

label: lemma-composition-module-flat
statement: Let $X \to Y \to Z$ be morphisms of schemes. Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a quasi-coherent $\mathcal{O}_X$-module. Let $x \in X$ with image $y$ in $Y$. If $\mathcal{F}$ is flat over $Y$ at $x$, and $Y$ is flat over $Z$ at $y$, then $\mathcal{F}$ is flat over $Z$ at $x$.

label: lemma-composition-flat
statement: The composition of flat morphisms is flat.

label: lemma-base-change-module-flat
statement: Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes. Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a quasi-coherent sheaf of $\mathcal{O}_X$-modules. Let $g : S' \to S$ be a morphism of schemes. Denote $g' : X' = X_{S'} \to X$ the projection. Let $x' \in X'$ be a point with image $x = g'(x') \in X$. If $\mathcal{F}$ is flat over $S$ at $x$, then $(g')^*\mathcal{F}$ is flat over $S'$ at $x'$. In particular, if $\mathcal{F}$ is flat over $S$, then $(g')^*\mathcal{F}$ is flat over $S'$.

label: lemma-base-change-flat
statement: The base change of a flat morphism is flat.

label: lemma-generalizations-lift-flat
statement: Let $f : X \to S$ be a flat morphism of schemes. Then generalizations lift along $f$, see Topology, Definition \ref{topology-definition-lift-specializations}.

label: lemma-fppf-open
statement: A flat morphism locally of finite presentation is universally open.

label: lemma-pf-flat-module-open
statement: Let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of schemes. Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a quasi-coherent $\mathcal{O}_X$-module. Assume $f$ locally finite presentation, $\mathcal{F}$ of finite type, $X = \text{Supp}(\mathcal{F})$, and $\mathcal{F}$ flat over $Y$. Then $f$ is universally open.

label: lemma-fpqc-quotient-topology
statement: Let $f : X \to Y$ be a quasi-compact, surjective, flat morphism. A subset $T \subset Y$ is open (resp.\ closed) if and only $f^{-1}(T)$ is open (resp.\ closed). In other words, $f$ is a submersive morphism.

label: lemma-flat-permanence
statement: Let $h : X \to Y$ be a morphism of schemes over $S$. Let $\mathcal{G}$ be a quasi-coherent sheaf on $Y$. Let $x \in X$ with $y = h(x) \in Y$. If $h$ is flat at $x$, then $$ \mathcal{G}\text{ flat over }S\text{ at }y \Leftrightarrow h^*\mathcal{G}\text{ flat over }S\text{ at }x. $$ In particular: If $h$ is surjective and flat, then $\mathcal{G}$ is flat over $S$, if and only if $h^*\mathcal{G}$ is flat over $S$. If $h$ is surjective and flat, and $X$ is flat over $S$, then $Y$ is flat over $S$.

label: lemma-flat-pullback-support
statement: Let $f : Y \to X$ be a morphism of schemes. Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a finite type quasi-coherent $\mathcal{O}_X$-module with scheme theoretic support $Z \subset X$. If $f$ is flat, then $f^{-1}(Z)$ is the scheme theoretic support of $f^*\mathcal{F}$.

label: lemma-flat-morphism-scheme-theoretically-dense-open
statement: Let $f : X \to Y$ be a flat morphism of schemes. Let $V \subset Y$ be a retrocompact open which is scheme theoretically dense. Then $f^{-1}V$ is scheme theoretically dense in $X$.

label: lemma-flat-base-change-scheme-theoretic-image
slogan: Taking scheme theoretic images commutes with flat base change in the quasi-compact case
statement: Let $f : X \to Y$ be a flat morphism of schemes. Let $g : V \to Y$ be a quasi-compact morphism of schemes. Let $Z \subset Y$ be the scheme theoretic image of $g$ and let $Z' \subset X$ be the scheme theoretic image of the base change $V \times_Y X \to X$. Then $Z' = f^{-1}Z$.

label: lemma-characterize-flat-closed-immersions
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme. The rule which associates to a closed subscheme of $X$ its underlying closed subset defines a bijection $$ \left\{ \begin{matrix} \text{closed subschemes }Z \subset X \\ \text{such that }Z \to X\text{ is flat} \end{matrix} \right\} \leftrightarrow \left\{ \begin{matrix} \text{closed subsets }Z \subset X \\ \text{closed under generalizations} \end{matrix} \right\} $$ If $Z \subset X$ is such a closed subscheme, every morphism of schemes $g : Y \to X$ with $g(Y) \subset Z$ set theoretically factors (scheme theoretically) through $Z$.

label: lemma-flat-closed-immersions-finite-presentation
statement: A flat closed immersion of finite presentation is the open immersion of an open and closed subscheme.

label: definition-scheme-structure-connected-component
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme. Let $T \subset X$ be a connected component. The {\it canonical scheme structure on $T$} is the unique scheme structure on $T$ such that the closed immersion $T \to X$ is flat, see Lemma \ref{lemma-characterize-flat-closed-immersions}.

label: lemma-finite-flat-is-finite-locally-free
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme. The following are equivalent every finite flat quasi-coherent $\mathcal{O}_X$-module is finite locally free, and every closed subset $Z \subset X$ which is closed under generalizations is open.

label: proposition-generic-flatness
title: Generic flatness
statement: Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes. Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a quasi-coherent sheaf of $\mathcal{O}_X$-modules. Assume $S$ is integral, $f$ is of finite type, and $\mathcal{F}$ is a finite type $\mathcal{O}_X$-module. Then there exists an open dense subscheme $U \subset S$ such that $X_U \to U$ is flat and of finite presentation and such that $\mathcal{F}|_{X_U}$ is flat over $U$ and of finite presentation over $\mathcal{O}_{X_U}$.

label: proposition-generic-flatness-reduced
title: Generic flatness, reduced case
statement: Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes. Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a quasi-coherent sheaf of $\mathcal{O}_X$-modules. Assume $S$ is reduced, $f$ is of finite type, and $\mathcal{F}$ is a finite type $\mathcal{O}_X$-module. Then there exists an open dense subscheme $U \subset S$ such that $X_U \to U$ is flat and of finite presentation and such that $\mathcal{F}|_{X_U}$ is flat over $U$ and of finite presentation over $\mathcal{O}_{X_U}$.

label: remark-flattening
statement: The results above are a first step towards more refined flattening techniques for morphisms of schemes. The article \cite{GruRay} by Raynaud and Gruson contains many wonderful results in this direction.

label: lemma-dimension-fibre-at-a-point
statement: Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes. Let $x \in X$ and set $s = f(x)$. Assume $f$ is locally of finite type. Then $$ \dim_x(X_s) = \dim(\mathcal{O}_{X_s, x}) + \text{trdeg}_{\kappa(s)}(\kappa(x)). $$

label: lemma-dimension-fibre-at-a-point-additive
statement: Let $f : X \to Y$ and $g : Y \to S$ be morphisms of schemes. Let $x \in X$ and set $y = f(x)$, $s = g(y)$. Assume $f$ and $g$ locally of finite type. Then $$ \dim_x(X_s) \leq \dim_x(X_y) + \dim_y(Y_s). $$ Moreover, equality holds if $\mathcal{O}_{X_s, x}$ is flat over $\mathcal{O}_{Y_s, y}$, which holds for example if $\mathcal{O}_{X, x}$ is flat over $\mathcal{O}_{Y, y}$.

label: lemma-dimension-fibre-after-base-change
statement: Let $$ \xymatrix{ X' \ar[r]_{g'} \ar[d]_{f'} & X \ar[d]^f \\ S' \ar[r]^g & S } $$ be a fibre product diagram of schemes. Assume $f$ locally of finite type. Suppose that $x' \in X'$, $x = g'(x')$, $s' = f'(x')$ and $s = g(s') = f(x)$. Then $\dim_x(X_s) = \dim_{x'}(X'_{s'})$, if $F$ is the fibre of the morphism $X'_{s'} \to X_s$ over $x$, then $$ \dim(\mathcal{O}_{F, x'}) = \dim(\mathcal{O}_{X'_{s'}, x'}) - \dim(\mathcal{O}_{X_s, x}) = \text{trdeg}_{\kappa(s)}(\kappa(x)) - \text{trdeg}_{\kappa(s')}(\kappa(x')) $$ In particular $\dim(\mathcal{O}_{X'_{s'}, x'}) \geq \dim(\mathcal{O}_{X_s, x})$ and $\text{trdeg}_{\kappa(s)}(\kappa(x)) \geq \text{trdeg}_{\kappa(s')}(\kappa(x'))$. given $s', s, x$ there exists a choice of $x'$ such that $\dim(\mathcal{O}_{X'_{s'}, x'}) = \dim(\mathcal{O}_{X_s, x})$ and $\text{trdeg}_{\kappa(s)}(\kappa(x)) = \text{trdeg}_{\kappa(s')}(\kappa(x'))$.

label: lemma-openness-bounded-dimension-fibres
statement: Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes. Let $n \geq 0$. Assume $f$ is locally of finite type. The set $$ U_n = \{x \in X \mid \dim_x X_{f(x)} \leq n\} $$ is open in $X$.

label: lemma-morphism-finite-type-bounded-dimension
statement: Let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of finite type with $Y$ quasi-compact. Then the dimension of the fibres of $f$ is bounded.

label: lemma-openness-bounded-dimension-fibres-finite-presentation
statement: Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes. Let $n \geq 0$. Assume $f$ is locally of finite presentation. The open $$ U_n = \{x \in X \mid \dim_x X_{f(x)} \leq n\} $$ of Lemma \ref{lemma-openness-bounded-dimension-fibres} is retrocompact in $X$. (See Topology, Definition \ref{topology-definition-quasi-compact}.)

label: lemma-dimension-fibre-specialization
statement: Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes. Let $x \leadsto x'$ be a nontrivial specialization of points in $X$ lying over the same point $s \in S$. Assume $f$ is locally of finite type. Then $\dim_x(X_s) \leq \dim_{x'}(X_s)$, $\dim(\mathcal{O}_{X_s, x}) < \dim(\mathcal{O}_{X_s, x'})$, and $\text{trdeg}_{\kappa(s)}(\kappa(x)) > \text{trdeg}_{\kappa(s)}(\kappa(x'))$.

label: definition-relative-dimension-d
statement: Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes. Assume $f$ is locally of finite type. We say $f$ is of {\it relative dimension $\leq d$ at $x$} if $\dim_x(X_{f(x)}) \leq d$. We say $f$ is of {\it relative dimension $\leq d$} if $\dim_x(X_{f(x)}) \leq d$ for all $x \in X$. We say $f$ is of {\it relative dimension $d$} if all nonempty fibres $X_s$ are equidimensional of dimension $d$.

label: lemma-base-change-relative-dimension-d
statement: Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes which is locally of finite type. If $f$ has relative dimension $d$, then so does any base change of $f$. Same for relative dimension $\leq d$.

label: lemma-composition-relative-dimension-d
statement: Let $f : X \to Y$, $g : Y \to Z$ be locally of finite type. If $f$ has relative dimension $\leq d$ and $g$ has relative dimension $\leq e$ then $g \circ f$ has relative dimension $\leq d + e$. If $f$ has relative dimension $d$, $g$ has relative dimension $e$, and $f$ is flat, then $g \circ f$ has relative dimension $d + e$.

label: lemma-flat-finite-presentation-CM-fibres-relative-dimension
slogan: Cohen-Macaulay morphisms decompose into clopens of pure relative dimension
statement: Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes. Assume that $f$ is flat, $f$ is locally of finite presentation, and for all $s \in S$ the fibre $X_s$ is Cohen-Macaulay (Properties, Definition \ref{properties-definition-Cohen-Macaulay}) Then there exist open and closed subschemes $X_d \subset X$ such that $X = \coprod_{d \geq 0} X_d$ and $f|_{X_d} : X_d \to S$ has relative dimension $d$.

label: lemma-locally-quasi-finite-rel-dimension-0
statement: Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes. Assume $f$ is locally of finite type. Let $x \in X$ with $s = f(x)$. Then $f$ is quasi-finite at $x$ if and only if $\dim_x(X_s) = 0$. In particular, $f$ is locally quasi-finite if and only if $f$ has relative dimension $0$.

label: lemma-rel-dimension-dimension
statement: Let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of locally Noetherian schemes which is flat, locally of finite type and of relative dimension $d$. For every point $x$ in $X$ with image $y$ in $Y$ we have $\dim_x(X) = \dim_y(Y) + d$.

label: definition-syntomic
statement: Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes. We say that $f$ is {\it syntomic at $x \in X$} if there exists an affine open neighbourhood $\Spec(A) = U \subset X$ of $x$ and affine open $\Spec(R) = V \subset S$ with $f(U) \subset V$ such that the induced ring map $R \to A$ is syntomic. We say that $f$ is {\it syntomic} if it is syntomic at every point of $X$. If $S = \Spec(k)$ and $f$ is syntomic, then we say that $X$ is a {\it local complete intersection over $k$}. A morphism of affine schemes $f : X \to S$ is called {\it standard syntomic} if there exists a global relative complete intersection $R \to R[x_1, \ldots, x_n]/(f_1, \ldots, f_c)$ (see Algebra, Definition \ref{algebra-definition-relative-global-complete-intersection}) such that $X \to S$ is isomorphic to $$ \Spec(R[x_1, \ldots, x_n]/(f_1, \ldots, f_c)) \to \Spec(R). $$

label: lemma-syntomic-characterize
statement: Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes. The following are equivalent The morphism $f$ is syntomic. For every affine opens $U \subset X$, $V \subset S$ with $f(U) \subset V$ the ring map $\mathcal{O}_S(V) \to \mathcal{O}_X(U)$ is syntomic. There exists an open covering $S = \bigcup_{j \in J} V_j$ and open coverings $f^{-1}(V_j) = \bigcup_{i \in I_j} U_i$ such that each of the morphisms $U_i \to V_j$, $j\in J, i\in I_j$ is syntomic. There exists an affine open covering $S = \bigcup_{j \in J} V_j$ and affine open coverings $f^{-1}(V_j) = \bigcup_{i \in I_j} U_i$ such that the ring map $\mathcal{O}_S(V_j) \to \mathcal{O}_X(U_i)$ is syntomic, for all $j\in J, i\in I_j$. Moreover, if $f$ is syntomic then for any open subschemes $U \subset X$, $V \subset S$ with $f(U) \subset V$ the restriction $f|_U : U \to V$ is syntomic.

label: lemma-composition-syntomic
statement: The composition of two morphisms which are syntomic is syntomic.

label: lemma-base-change-syntomic
statement: The base change of a morphism which is syntomic is syntomic.

label: lemma-open-immersion-syntomic
statement: Any open immersion is syntomic.

label: lemma-syntomic-locally-finite-presentation
statement: A syntomic morphism is locally of finite presentation.

label: lemma-syntomic-flat
statement: A syntomic morphism is flat.

label: lemma-syntomic-open
statement: A syntomic morphism is universally open.

label: lemma-local-complete-intersection
statement: Let $k$ be a field. Let $X$ be a scheme locally of finite type over $k$. The following are equivalent: $X$ is a local complete intersection over $k$, for every $x \in X$ there exists an affine open $U = \Spec(R) \subset X$ neighbourhood of $x$ such that $R \cong k[x_1, \ldots, x_n]/(f_1, \ldots, f_c)$ is a global complete intersection over $k$, and for every $x \in X$ the local ring $\mathcal{O}_{X, x}$ is a complete intersection over $k$.

label: lemma-syntomic-locally-standard-syntomic
statement: Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes. Let $x \in X$ be a point with image $s = f(x)$. Let $V \subset S$ be an affine open neighbourhood of $s$. The following are equivalent The morphism $f$ is syntomic at $x$. There exist an affine open $U \subset X$ with $x \in U$ and $f(U) \subset V$ such that $f|_U : U \to V$ is standard syntomic. The morphism $f$ is of finite presentation at $x$, the local ring map $\mathcal{O}_{S, s} \to \mathcal{O}_{X, x}$ is flat and $\mathcal{O}_{X, x}/\mathfrak m_s \mathcal{O}_{X, x}$ is a complete intersection over $\kappa(s)$ (see Algebra, Definition \ref{algebra-definition-lci-local-ring}).

label: lemma-syntomic-flat-fibres
statement: Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes. If $f$ is flat, locally of finite presentation, and all fibres $X_s$ are local complete intersections, then $f$ is syntomic.

label: lemma-set-points-where-fibres-lci
statement: Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes. Assume $f$ locally of finite type. Formation of the set $$ T = \{x \in X \mid \mathcal{O}_{X_{f(x)}, x} \text{ is a complete intersection over }\kappa(f(x))\} $$ commutes with arbitrary base change: For any morphism $g : S' \to S$, consider the base change $f' : X' \to S'$ of $f$ and the projection $g' : X' \to X$. Then the corresponding set $T'$ for the morphism $f'$ is equal to $T' = (g')^{-1}(T)$. In particular, if $f$ is assumed flat, and locally of finite presentation then the same holds for the open set of points where $f$ is syntomic.

label: lemma-standard-syntomic-relative-dimension
statement: Let $R$ be a ring. Let $R \to A = R[x_1, \ldots, x_n]/(f_1, \ldots, f_c)$ be a relative global complete intersection. Set $S = \Spec(R)$ and $X = \Spec(A)$. Consider the morphism $f : X \to S$ associated to the ring map $R \to A$. The function $x \mapsto \dim_x(X_{f(x)})$ is constant with value $n - c$.

label: lemma-syntomic-relative-dimension
statement: Let $f : X \to S$ be a syntomic morphism. The function $x \mapsto \dim_x(X_{f(x)})$ is locally constant on $X$.

label: definition-syntomic-relative-dimension
statement: Let $d \geq 0$ be an integer. We say a morphism of schemes $f : X \to S$ is {\it syntomic of relative dimension $d$} if $f$ is syntomic and the function $\dim_x(X_{f(x)}) = d$ for all $x \in X$.

label: lemma-syntomic-permanence
statement: Let $$ \xymatrix{ X \ar[rr]_f \ar[rd]_p & & Y \ar[dl]^q \\ & S } $$ be a commutative diagram of morphisms of schemes. Assume that $f$ is surjective and syntomic, $p$ is syntomic, and $q$ is locally of finite presentation\footnote{In fact, if $f$ is surjective, flat, and locally of finite presentation and $p$ is syntomic, then both $q$ and $f$ are syntomic, see Descent, Lemma \ref{descent-lemma-syntomic-permanence}.}. Then $q$ is syntomic.

label: definition-conormal-sheaf
statement: Let $i : Z \to X$ be an immersion. The {\it conormal sheaf $\mathcal{C}_{Z/X}$ of $Z$ in $X$} or the {\it conormal sheaf of $i$} is the quasi-coherent $\mathcal{O}_Z$-module $\mathcal{I}/\mathcal{I}^2$ described above.

label: lemma-affine-conormal
statement: Let $i : Z \to X$ be an immersion. The conormal sheaf of $i$ has the following properties: Let $U \subset X$ be any open subscheme such that $i$ factors as $Z \xrightarrow{i'} U \to X$ where $i'$ is a closed immersion. Let $\mathcal{I} = \Ker((i')^\sharp) \subset \mathcal{O}_U$. Then $$ \mathcal{C}_{Z/X} = (i')^*\mathcal{I}\quad\text{and}\quad i'_*\mathcal{C}_{Z/X} = \mathcal{I}/\mathcal{I}^2 $$ For any affine open $\Spec(R) = U \subset X$ such that $Z \cap U = \Spec(R/I)$ there is a canonical isomorphism $\Gamma(Z \cap U, \mathcal{C}_{Z/X}) = I/I^2$.

label: lemma-conormal-functorial
statement: Let $$ \xymatrix{ Z \ar[r]_i \ar[d]_f & X \ar[d]^g \\ Z' \ar[r]^{i'} & X' } $$ be a commutative diagram in the category of schemes. Assume $i$, $i'$ immersions. There is a canonical map of $\mathcal{O}_Z$-modules $$ f^*\mathcal{C}_{Z'/X'} \longrightarrow \mathcal{C}_{Z/X} $$ characterized by the following property: For every pair of affine opens $(\Spec(R) = U \subset X, \Spec(R') = U' \subset X')$ with $g(U) \subset U'$ such that $Z \cap U = \Spec(R/I)$ and $Z' \cap U' = \Spec(R'/I')$ the induced map $$ \Gamma(Z' \cap U', \mathcal{C}_{Z'/X'}) = I'/I'^2 \longrightarrow I/I^2 = \Gamma(Z \cap U, \mathcal{C}_{Z/X}) $$ is the one induced by the ring map $g^\sharp : R' \to R$ which has the property $g^\sharp(I') \subset I$.

label: lemma-conormal-functorial-flat
statement: Let $$ \xymatrix{ Z \ar[r]_i \ar[d]_f & X \ar[d]^g \\ Z' \ar[r]^{i'} & X' } $$ be a fibre product diagram in the category of schemes with $i$, $i'$ immersions. Then the canonical map $f^*\mathcal{C}_{Z'/X'} \to \mathcal{C}_{Z/X}$ of Lemma \ref{lemma-conormal-functorial} is surjective. If $g$ is flat, then it is an isomorphism.

label: lemma-transitivity-conormal
statement: Let $Z \to Y \to X$ be immersions of schemes. Then there is a canonical exact sequence $$ i^*\mathcal{C}_{Y/X} \to \mathcal{C}_{Z/X} \to \mathcal{C}_{Z/Y} \to 0 $$ where the maps come from Lemma \ref{lemma-conormal-functorial} and $i : Z \to Y$ is the first morphism.

label: definition-sheaf-differentials
section: Sheaf of differentials of a morphism
statement: Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes. The {\it sheaf of differentials $\Omega_{X/S}$ of $X$ over $S$} is the sheaf of differentials of $f$ viewed as a morphism of ringed spaces (Modules, Definition \ref{modules-definition-differentials}) equipped with its {\it universal $S$-derivation} $$ \text{d}_{X/S} : \mathcal{O}_X \longrightarrow \Omega_{X/S}. $$

label: lemma-universal-derivation-universal
section: Sheaf of differentials of a morphism
statement: Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes. The map $$ \Hom_{\mathcal{O}_X}(\Omega_{X/S}, \mathcal{F}) \longrightarrow \text{Der}_S(\mathcal{O}_X, \mathcal{F}),\quad \alpha \longmapsto \alpha \circ \text{d}_{X/S} $$ is an isomorphism of functors $\textit{Mod}(\mathcal{O}_X) \to \textit{Sets}$.

label: lemma-differentials-restrict-open
section: Sheaf of differentials of a morphism
statement: Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes. Let $U \subset X$, $V \subset S$ be open subschemes such that $f(U) \subset V$. Then there is a unique isomorphism $\Omega_{X/S}|_U = \Omega_{U/V}$ of $\mathcal{O}_U$-modules such that $\text{d}_{X/S}|_U = \text{d}_{U/V}$.

label: lemma-affine-case-derivation
section: Sheaf of differentials of a morphism
statement: Let $R \to A$ be a ring map. Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a sheaf of $\mathcal{O}_X$-modules on $X = \Spec(A)$. Set $S = \Spec(R)$. The rule which associates to an $S$-derivation on $\mathcal{F}$ its action on global sections defines a bijection between the set of $S$-derivations of $\mathcal{F}$ and the set of $R$-derivations on $M = \Gamma(X, \mathcal{F})$.

label: lemma-differentials-affine
section: Sheaf of differentials of a morphism
statement: Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes. For any pair of affine opens $\Spec(A) = U \subset X$, $\Spec(R) = V \subset S$ with $f(U) \subset V$ there is a unique isomorphism $$ \Gamma(U, \Omega_{X/S}) = \Omega_{A/R}. $$ compatible with $\text{d}_{X/S}$ and $\text{d} : A \to \Omega_{A/R}$.

label: remark-differentials-glue
section: Sheaf of differentials of a morphism
statement: The lemma above gives a second way of constructing the module of differentials. Namely, let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes. Consider the collection of all affine opens $U \subset X$ which map into an affine open of $S$. These form a basis for the topology on $X$. Thus it suffices to define $\Gamma(U, \Omega_{X/S})$ for such $U$. We simply set $\Gamma(U, \Omega_{X/S}) = \Omega_{A/R}$ if $A$, $R$ are as in Lemma \ref{lemma-differentials-affine} above. This works, but it takes somewhat more algebraic preliminaries to construct the restriction mappings and to verify the sheaf condition with this ansatz.

label: lemma-differentials-diagonal
section: Sheaf of differentials of a morphism
statement: Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes. There is a canonical isomorphism between $\Omega_{X/S}$ and the conormal sheaf of the diagonal morphism $\Delta_{X/S} : X \longrightarrow X \times_S X$.

label: lemma-functoriality-differentials
section: Sheaf of differentials of a morphism
statement: Let $$ \xymatrix{ X' \ar[d] \ar[r]_f & X \ar[d] \\ S' \ar[r] & S } $$ be a commutative diagram of schemes. The canonical map $\mathcal{O}_X \to f_*\mathcal{O}_{X'}$ composed with the map $f_*\text{d}_{X'/S'} : f_*\mathcal{O}_{X'} \to f_*\Omega_{X'/S'}$ is a $S$-derivation. Hence we obtain a canonical map of $\mathcal{O}_X$-modules $\Omega_{X/S} \to f_*\Omega_{X'/S'}$, and by adjointness of $f_*$ and $f^*$ a canonical $\mathcal{O}_{X'}$-module homomorphism $$ c_f : f^*\Omega_{X/S} \longrightarrow \Omega_{X'/S'}. $$ It is uniquely characterized by the property that $f^*\text{d}_{X/S}(h)$ maps to $\text{d}_{X'/S'}(f^* h)$ for any local section $h$ of $\mathcal{O}_X$.

label: lemma-triangle-differentials
section: Sheaf of differentials of a morphism
statement: Let $f : X \to Y$, $g : Y \to S$ be morphisms of schemes. Then there is a canonical exact sequence $$ f^*\Omega_{Y/S} \to \Omega_{X/S} \to \Omega_{X/Y} \to 0 $$ where the maps come from applications of Lemma \ref{lemma-functoriality-differentials}.

label: lemma-base-change-differentials
section: Sheaf of differentials of a morphism
statement: Let $X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes. Let $g : S' \to S$ be a morphism of schemes. Let $X' = X_{S'}$ be the base change of $X$. Denote $g' : X' \to X$ the projection. Then the map $$ (g')^*\Omega_{X/S} \to \Omega_{X'/S'} $$ of Lemma \ref{lemma-functoriality-differentials} is an isomorphism.

label: lemma-differential-product
section: Sheaf of differentials of a morphism
statement: Let $f : X \to S$ and $g : Y \to S$ be morphisms of schemes with the same target. Let $p : X \times_S Y \to X$ and $q : X \times_S Y \to Y$ be the projection morphisms. The maps from Lemma \ref{lemma-functoriality-differentials} $$ p^*\Omega_{X/S} \oplus q^*\Omega_{Y/S} \longrightarrow \Omega_{X \times_S Y/S} $$ give an isomorphism.

label: lemma-finite-type-differentials
section: Sheaf of differentials of a morphism
statement: Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes. If $f$ is locally of finite type, then $\Omega_{X/S}$ is a finite type $\mathcal{O}_X$-module.

label: lemma-finite-presentation-differentials
section: Sheaf of differentials of a morphism
statement: Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes. If $f$ is locally of finite presentation, then $\Omega_{X/S}$ is an $\mathcal{O}_X$-module of finite presentation.

label: lemma-immersion-differentials
section: Sheaf of differentials of a morphism
statement: If $X \to S$ is an immersion, or more generally a monomorphism, then $\Omega_{X/S}$ is zero.

label: lemma-differentials-relative-immersion
section: Sheaf of differentials of a morphism
statement: Let $i : Z \to X$ be an immersion of schemes over $S$. There is a canonical exact sequence $$ \mathcal{C}_{Z/X} \to i^*\Omega_{X/S} \to \Omega_{Z/S} \to 0 $$ where the first arrow is induced by $\text{d}_{X/S}$ and the second arrow comes from Lemma \ref{lemma-functoriality-differentials}.

label: lemma-differentials-relative-immersion-section
section: Sheaf of differentials of a morphism
statement: Let $i : Z \to X$ be an immersion of schemes over $S$, and assume $i$ (locally) has a left inverse. Then the canonical sequence $$ 0 \to \mathcal{C}_{Z/X} \to i^*\Omega_{X/S} \to \Omega_{Z/S} \to 0 $$ of Lemma \ref{lemma-differentials-relative-immersion} is (locally) split exact. In particular, if $s : S \to X$ is a section of the structure morphism $X \to S$ then the map $\mathcal{C}_{S/X} \to s^*\Omega_{X/S}$ induced by $\text{d}_{X/S}$ is an isomorphism.

label: remark-differentials-diagonal
section: Sheaf of differentials of a morphism
statement: Let $X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes. According to Lemma \ref{lemma-differential-product} we have $$ \Omega_{X \times_S X/S} = \text{pr}_1^*\Omega_{X/S} \oplus \text{pr}_2^*\Omega_{X/S} $$ On the other hand, the diagonal morphism $\Delta : X \to X \times_S X$ is an immersion, which locally has a left inverse. Hence by Lemma \ref{lemma-differentials-relative-immersion-section} we obtain a canonical short exact sequence $$ 0 \to \mathcal{C}_{X/X \times_S X} \to \Omega_{X/S} \oplus \Omega_{X/S} \to \Omega_{X/S} \to 0 $$ Note that the right arrow is $(1, 1)$ which is indeed a split surjection. On the other hand, by Lemma \ref{lemma-differentials-diagonal} we have an identification $\Omega_{X/S} = \mathcal{C}_{X/X \times_S X}$. Because we chose $\text{d}_{X/S}(f) = s_2(f) - s_1(f)$ in this identification it turns out that the left arrow is the map $(-1, 1)$\footnote{Namely, the local section $\text{d}_{X/S}(f) = 1 \otimes f - f \otimes 1$ of the ideal sheaf of $\Delta$ maps via $\text{d}_{X \times_S X/X}$ to the local section $1 \otimes 1 \otimes 1 \otimes f - 1 \otimes f \otimes 1 \otimes 1 -1 \otimes 1 \otimes f \otimes 1 + f \otimes 1 \otimes 1 \otimes 1 = \text{pr}_2^*\text{d}_{X/S}(f) - \text{pr}_1^*\text{d}_{X/S}(f)$.}.

label: lemma-two-immersions
section: Sheaf of differentials of a morphism
statement: Let $$ \xymatrix{ Z \ar[r]_i \ar[rd]_j & X \ar[d] \\ & Y } $$ be a commutative diagram of schemes where $i$ and $j$ are immersions. Then there is a canonical exact sequence $$ \mathcal{C}_{Z/Y} \to \mathcal{C}_{Z/X} \to i^*\Omega_{X/Y} \to 0 $$ where the first arrow comes from Lemma \ref{lemma-conormal-functorial} and the second from Lemma \ref{lemma-differentials-relative-immersion}.

label: lemma-affine-case-differential-operators
statement: Let $R \to A$ be a ring map. Denote $f : X \to S$ the corresponding morphism of affine schemes. Let $\mathcal{F}$ and $\mathcal{G}$ be $\mathcal{O}_X$-modules. If $\mathcal{F}$ is quasi-coherent then the map $$ \text{Diff}^k_{X/S}(\mathcal{F}, \mathcal{G}) \to \text{Diff}^k_{A/R}(\Gamma(X, \mathcal{F}), \Gamma(X, \mathcal{G})) $$ sending a differential operator to its action on global sections is bijective.

label: lemma-base-change-differential-operators
statement: Let $a : X \to S$ and $b : Y \to S$ be morphisms of schemes. Let $\mathcal{F}$ and $\mathcal{F}'$ be quasi-coherent $\mathcal{O}_X$-modules. Let $D : \mathcal{F} \to \mathcal{F}'$ be a differential operator of order $k$ on $X/S$. Let $\mathcal{G}$ be a quasi-coherent $\mathcal{O}_Y$-module. Then there is a unique differential operator $$ D' : \text{pr}_1^*\mathcal{F} \otimes_{\mathcal{O}_{X \times_S Y}} \text{pr}_2^*\mathcal{G} \longrightarrow \text{pr}_1^*\mathcal{F}' \otimes_{\mathcal{O}_{X \times_S Y}} \text{pr}_2^*\mathcal{G} $$ of order $k$ on $X \times_S Y / Y$ such that $ D'(s \otimes t) = D(s) \otimes t $ for local sections $s$ of $\mathcal{F}$ and $t$ of $\mathcal{G}$.

label: remark-base-change-differential-operators
statement: Let $a : X \to S$ and $b : Y \to S$ be morphisms of schemes. Denote $p : X \times_S Y \to X$ and $q : X \times_S Y \to Y$ the projections. In this remark, given an $\mathcal{O}_X$-module $\mathcal{F}$ and an $\mathcal{O}_Y$-module $\mathcal{G}$ let us set $$ \mathcal{F} \boxtimes \mathcal{G} = p^*\mathcal{F} \otimes_{\mathcal{O}_{X \times_S Y}} q^*\mathcal{G} $$ Denote $\mathcal{A}_{X/S}$ the additive category whose objects are quasi-coherent $\mathcal{O}_X$-modules and whose morphisms are differential operators of finite order on $X/S$. Similarly for $\mathcal{A}_{Y/S}$ and $\mathcal{A}_{X \times_S Y/S}$. The construction of Lemma \ref{lemma-base-change-differential-operators} determines a functor $$ \boxtimes : \mathcal{A}_{X/S} \times \mathcal{A}_{Y/S} \longrightarrow \mathcal{A}_{X \times_S Y/S}, \quad (\mathcal{F}, \mathcal{G}) \longmapsto \mathcal{F} \boxtimes \mathcal{G} $$ which is bilinear on morphisms. If $X = \Spec(A)$, $Y = \Spec(B)$, and $S = \Spec(R)$, then via the identification of quasi-coherent sheaves with modules this functor is given by $(M, N) \mapsto M \otimes_R N$ on objects and sends the morphism $(D, D') : (M, N) \to (M', N')$ to $D \otimes D' : M \otimes_R N \to M' \otimes_R N'$.

label: definition-smooth
statement: Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes. We say that $f$ is {\it smooth at $x \in X$} if there exist an affine open neighbourhood $\Spec(A) = U \subset X$ of $x$ and affine open $\Spec(R) = V \subset S$ with $f(U) \subset V$ such that the induced ring map $R \to A$ is smooth. We say that $f$ is {\it smooth} if it is smooth at every point of $X$. A morphism of affine schemes $f : X \to S$ is called {\it standard smooth} if there exists a standard smooth ring map $R \to R[x_1, \ldots, x_n]/(f_1, \ldots, f_c)$ (see Algebra, Definition \ref{algebra-definition-standard-smooth}) such that $X \to S$ is isomorphic to $$ \Spec(R[x_1, \ldots, x_n]/(f_1, \ldots, f_c)) \to \Spec(R). $$

label: lemma-smooth-characterize
statement: Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes. The following are equivalent The morphism $f$ is smooth. For every affine opens $U \subset X$, $V \subset S$ with $f(U) \subset V$ the ring map $\mathcal{O}_S(V) \to \mathcal{O}_X(U)$ is smooth. There exists an open covering $S = \bigcup_{j \in J} V_j$ and open coverings $f^{-1}(V_j) = \bigcup_{i \in I_j} U_i$ such that each of the morphisms $U_i \to V_j$, $j\in J, i\in I_j$ is smooth. There exists an affine open covering $S = \bigcup_{j \in J} V_j$ and affine open coverings $f^{-1}(V_j) = \bigcup_{i \in I_j} U_i$ such that the ring map $\mathcal{O}_S(V_j) \to \mathcal{O}_X(U_i)$ is smooth, for all $j\in J, i\in I_j$. Moreover, if $f$ is smooth then for any open subschemes $U \subset X$, $V \subset S$ with $f(U) \subset V$ the restriction $f|_U : U \to V$ is smooth.

label: lemma-smooth-flat-smooth-fibres
statement: Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes. If $f$ is flat, locally of finite presentation, and all fibres $X_s$ are smooth, then $f$ is smooth.

label: lemma-composition-smooth
statement: The composition of two morphisms which are smooth is smooth.

label: lemma-base-change-smooth
statement: The base change of a morphism which is smooth is smooth.

label: lemma-open-immersion-smooth
statement: Any open immersion is smooth.

label: lemma-smooth-syntomic
statement: A smooth morphism is syntomic.

label: lemma-smooth-locally-finite-presentation
statement: A smooth morphism is locally of finite presentation.

label: lemma-smooth-flat
statement: A smooth morphism is flat.

label: lemma-smooth-open
statement: A smooth morphism is universally open.

label: lemma-smooth-locally-standard-smooth
slogan: Smooth morphisms are locally standard smooth.
statement: Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes. Let $x \in X$ be a point. Let $V \subset S$ be an affine open neighbourhood of $f(x)$. The following are equivalent The morphism $f$ is smooth at $x$. There exists an affine open $U \subset X$, with $x \in U$ and $f(U) \subset V$ such that the induced morphism $f|_U : U \to V$ is standard smooth.

label: lemma-smooth-omega-finite-locally-free
statement: Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes. Assume $f$ is smooth. Then the module of differentials $\Omega_{X/S}$ of $X$ over $S$ is finite locally free and $$ \text{rank}_x(\Omega_{X/S}) = \dim_x(X_{f(x)}) $$ for every $x \in X$.

label: definition-smooth-relative-dimension
statement: Let $d \geq 0$ be an integer. We say a morphism of schemes $f : X \to S$ is {\it smooth of relative dimension $d$} if $f$ is smooth and $\Omega_{X/S}$ is finite locally free of constant rank $d$.

label: lemma-smooth-at-point
statement: Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes. Let $x \in X$. Set $s = f(x)$. Assume $f$ is locally of finite presentation. The following are equivalent: The morphism $f$ is smooth at $x$. The local ring map $\mathcal{O}_{S, s} \to \mathcal{O}_{X, x}$ is flat and $X_s \to \Spec(\kappa(s))$ is smooth at $x$. The local ring map $\mathcal{O}_{S, s} \to \mathcal{O}_{X, x}$ is flat and the $\mathcal{O}_{X, x}$-module $\Omega_{X/S, x}$ can be generated by at most $\dim_x(X_{f(x)})$ elements. The local ring map $\mathcal{O}_{S, s} \to \mathcal{O}_{X, x}$ is flat and the $\kappa(x)$-vector space $$ \Omega_{X_s/s, x} \otimes_{\mathcal{O}_{X_s, x}} \kappa(x) = \Omega_{X/S, x} \otimes_{\mathcal{O}_{X, x}} \kappa(x) $$ can be generated by at most $\dim_x(X_{f(x)})$ elements. There exist affine opens $U \subset X$, and $V \subset S$ such that $x \in U$, $f(U) \subset V$ and the induced morphism $f|_U : U \to V$ is standard smooth. There exist affine opens $\Spec(A) = U \subset X$ and $\Spec(R) = V \subset S$ with $x \in U$ corresponding to $\mathfrak q \subset A$, and $f(U) \subset V$ such that there exists a presentation $$ A = R[x_1, \ldots, x_n]/(f_1, \ldots, f_c) $$ with $$ g = \det \left( \begin{matrix} \partial f_1/\partial x_1 & \partial f_2/\partial x_1 & \ldots & \partial f_c/\partial x_1 \\ \partial f_1/\partial x_2 & \partial f_2/\partial x_2 & \ldots & \partial f_c/\partial x_2 \\ \ldots & \ldots & \ldots & \ldots \\ \partial f_1/\partial x_c & \partial f_2/\partial x_c & \ldots & \partial f_c/\partial x_c \end{matrix} \right) $$ mapping to an element of $A$ not in $\mathfrak q$.

label: lemma-set-points-where-fibres-smooth
statement: Let $$ \xymatrix{ X' \ar[r]_{g'} \ar[d]_{f'} & X \ar[d]^f \\ S' \ar[r]^g & S } $$ be a cartesian diagram of schemes. Let $W \subset X$, resp.\ $W' \subset X'$ be the open subscheme of points where $f$, resp.\ $f'$ is smooth. Then $W' = (g')^{-1}(W)$ if $f$ is flat and locally of finite presentation, or $f$ is locally of finite presentation and $g$ is flat.

label: lemma-triangle-differentials-smooth
statement: Let $f : X \to Y$, $g : Y \to S$ be morphisms of schemes. Assume $f$ is smooth. Then $$ 0 \to f^*\Omega_{Y/S} \to \Omega_{X/S} \to \Omega_{X/Y} \to 0 $$ (see Lemma \ref{lemma-triangle-differentials}) is short exact.

label: lemma-differentials-relative-immersion-smooth
statement: Let $i : Z \to X$ be an immersion of schemes over $S$. Assume that $Z$ is smooth over $S$. Then the canonical exact sequence $$ 0 \to \mathcal{C}_{Z/X} \to i^*\Omega_{X/S} \to \Omega_{Z/S} \to 0 $$ of Lemma \ref{lemma-differentials-relative-immersion} is short exact.

label: lemma-two-immersions-smooth
statement: Let $$ \xymatrix{ Z \ar[r]_i \ar[rd]_j & X \ar[d] \\ & Y } $$ be a commutative diagram of schemes where $i$ and $j$ are immersions and $X \to Y$ is smooth. Then the canonical exact sequence $$ 0 \to \mathcal{C}_{Z/Y} \to \mathcal{C}_{Z/X} \to i^*\Omega_{X/Y} \to 0 $$ of Lemma \ref{lemma-two-immersions} is exact.

label: lemma-smooth-permanence
statement: Let $$ \xymatrix{ X \ar[rr]_f \ar[rd]_p & & Y \ar[dl]^q \\ & S } $$ be a commutative diagram of morphisms of schemes. Assume that $f$ is surjective, and smooth, $p$ is smooth, and $q$ is locally of finite presentation\footnote{In fact this is implied by (1) and (2), see Descent, Lemma \ref{descent-lemma-flat-finitely-presented-permanence}. Moreover, it suffices to assume $f$ is surjective, flat and locally of finite presentation, see Descent, Lemma \ref{descent-lemma-smooth-permanence}.}. Then $q$ is smooth.

label: lemma-section-smooth-morphism
statement: Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes. Let $\sigma : S \to X$ be a section of $f$. Let $s \in S$ be a point such that $f$ is smooth at $x = \sigma(s)$. Then there exist affine open neighbourhoods $\Spec(A) = U \subset S$ of $s$ and $\Spec(B) = V \subset X$ of $x$ such that $f(V) \subset U$ and $\sigma(U) \subset V$, with $I = \Ker(\sigma^\# : B \to A)$ the module $I/I^2$ is a free $A$-module, and $B^\wedge \cong A[[x_1, \ldots, x_d]]$ as $A$-algebras where $B^\wedge$ denotes the completion of $B$ with respect to $I$.

label: lemma-smoothness-dimension
statement: Let $f : X \to Y$ be a smooth morphism of locally Noetherian schemes. For every point $x$ in $X$ with image $y$ in $Y$, $$ \dim_x(X) = \dim_y(Y) + \dim_x(X_y), $$ where $X_y$ denotes the fiber over $y$.

label: definition-unramified
statement: Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes. We say that $f$ is {\it unramified at $x \in X$} if there exists an affine open neighbourhood $\Spec(A) = U \subset X$ of $x$ and affine open $\Spec(R) = V \subset S$ with $f(U) \subset V$ such that the induced ring map $R \to A$ is unramified. We say that $f$ is {\it G-unramified at $x \in X$} if there exists an affine open neighbourhood $\Spec(A) = U \subset X$ of $x$ and affine open $\Spec(R) = V \subset S$ with $f(U) \subset V$ such that the induced ring map $R \to A$ is G-unramified. We say that $f$ is {\it unramified} if it is unramified at every point of $X$. We say that $f$ is {\it G-unramified} if it is G-unramified at every point of $X$.

label: lemma-unramified-omega-zero
statement: Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes. Then $f$ is unramified if and only if $f$ is locally of finite type and $\Omega_{X/S} = 0$, and $f$ is G-unramified if and only if $f$ is locally of finite presentation and $\Omega_{X/S} = 0$.

label: lemma-unramified-characterize
statement: Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes. The following are equivalent The morphism $f$ is unramified (resp.\ G-unramified). For every affine open $U \subset X$, $V \subset S$ with $f(U) \subset V$ the ring map $\mathcal{O}_S(V) \to \mathcal{O}_X(U)$ is unramified (resp.\ G-unramified). There exists an open covering $S = \bigcup_{j \in J} V_j$ and open coverings $f^{-1}(V_j) = \bigcup_{i \in I_j} U_i$ such that each of the morphisms $U_i \to V_j$, $j\in J, i\in I_j$ is unramified (resp.\ G-unramified). There exists an affine open covering $S = \bigcup_{j \in J} V_j$ and affine open coverings $f^{-1}(V_j) = \bigcup_{i \in I_j} U_i$ such that the ring map $\mathcal{O}_S(V_j) \to \mathcal{O}_X(U_i)$ is unramified (resp.\ G-unramified), for all $j\in J, i\in I_j$. Moreover, if $f$ is unramified (resp.\ G-unramified) then for any open subschemes $U \subset X$, $V \subset S$ with $f(U) \subset V$ the restriction $f|_U : U \to V$ is unramified (resp.\ G-unramified).

label: lemma-composition-unramified
statement: The composition of two morphisms which are unramified is unramified. The same holds for G-unramified morphisms.

label: lemma-base-change-unramified
statement: The base change of a morphism which is unramified is unramified. The same holds for G-unramified morphisms.

label: lemma-noetherian-unramified
statement: Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes. Assume $S$ is locally Noetherian. Then $f$ is unramified if and only if $f$ is G-unramified.

label: lemma-open-immersion-unramified
statement: Any open immersion is G-unramified.

label: lemma-closed-immersion-unramified
statement: A closed immersion $i : Z \to X$ is unramified. It is G-unramified if and only if the associated quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals $\mathcal{I} = \Ker(\mathcal{O}_X \to i_*\mathcal{O}_Z)$ is of finite type (as an $\mathcal{O}_X$-module).

label: lemma-unramified-locally-finite-type
statement: An unramified morphism is locally of finite type. A G-unramified morphism is locally of finite presentation.

label: lemma-unramified-quasi-finite
statement: Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes. If $f$ is unramified at $x$ then $f$ is quasi-finite at $x$. In particular, an unramified morphism is locally quasi-finite.

label: lemma-unramified-over-field
statement: Fibres of unramified morphisms. Let $X$ be a scheme over a field $k$. The structure morphism $X \to \Spec(k)$ is unramified if and only if $X$ is a disjoint union of spectra of finite separable field extensions of $k$. If $f : X \to S$ is an unramified morphism then for every $s \in S$ the fibre $X_s$ is a disjoint union of spectra of finite separable field extensions of $\kappa(s)$.

label: lemma-unramified-etale-fibres
statement: Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes. If $f$ is unramified then for any $x \in X$ the field extension $\kappa(x)/\kappa(f(x))$ is finite separable. If $f$ is locally of finite type, and for every $s \in S$ the fibre $X_s$ is a disjoint union of spectra of finite separable field extensions of $\kappa(s)$ then $f$ is unramified. If $f$ is locally of finite presentation, and for every $s \in S$ the fibre $X_s$ is a disjoint union of spectra of finite separable field extensions of $\kappa(s)$ then $f$ is G-unramified.

label: lemma-diagonal-unramified-morphism
statement: Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism. If $f$ is unramified, then the diagonal morphism $\Delta : X \to X \times_S X$ is an open immersion. If $f$ is locally of finite type and $\Delta$ is an open immersion, then $f$ is unramified. If $f$ is locally of finite presentation and $\Delta$ is an open immersion, then $f$ is G-unramified.

label: lemma-unramified-at-point
statement: Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes. Let $x \in X$. Set $s = f(x)$. Assume $f$ is locally of finite type (resp.\ locally of finite presentation). The following are equivalent: The morphism $f$ is unramified (resp.\ G-unramified) at $x$. The fibre $X_s$ is unramified over $\kappa(s)$ at $x$. The $\mathcal{O}_{X, x}$-module $\Omega_{X/S, x}$ is zero. The $\mathcal{O}_{X_s, x}$-module $\Omega_{X_s/s, x}$ is zero. The $\kappa(x)$-vector space $$ \Omega_{X_s/s, x} \otimes_{\mathcal{O}_{X_s, x}} \kappa(x) = \Omega_{X/S, x} \otimes_{\mathcal{O}_{X, x}} \kappa(x) $$ is zero. We have $\mathfrak m_s\mathcal{O}_{X, x} = \mathfrak m_x$ and the field extension $\kappa(x)/\kappa(s)$ is finite separable.

label: lemma-set-points-where-fibres-unramified
statement: Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes. Assume $f$ locally of finite type. Formation of the open set \begin{align*} T & = \{x \in X \mid X_{f(x)}\text{ is unramified over }\kappa(f(x))\text{ at }x\} \\ & = \{x \in X \mid X\text{ is unramified over }S\text{ at }x\} \end{align*} commutes with arbitrary base change: For any morphism $g : S' \to S$, consider the base change $f' : X' \to S'$ of $f$ and the projection $g' : X' \to X$. Then the corresponding set $T'$ for the morphism $f'$ is equal to $T' = (g')^{-1}(T)$. If $f$ is assumed locally of finite presentation then the same holds for the open set of points where $f$ is G-unramified.

label: lemma-unramified-permanence
statement: Let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of schemes over $S$. If $X$ is unramified over $S$, then $f$ is unramified. If $X$ is G-unramified over $S$ and $Y$ is locally of finite type over $S$, then $f$ is G-unramified.

label: lemma-value-at-one-point
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $X$, $Y$ be schemes over $S$. Let $f, g : X \to Y$ be morphisms over $S$. Let $x \in X$. Assume that the structure morphism $Y \to S$ is unramified, $f(x) = g(x)$ in $Y$, say $y = f(x) = g(x)$, and the induced maps $f^\sharp, g^\sharp : \kappa(y) \to \kappa(x)$ are equal. Then there exists an open neighbourhood of $x$ in $X$ on which $f$ and $g$ are equal.

label: definition-etale
statement: Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes. We say that $f$ is {\it \'etale at $x \in X$} if there exists an affine open neighbourhood $\Spec(A) = U \subset X$ of $x$ and affine open $\Spec(R) = V \subset S$ with $f(U) \subset V$ such that the induced ring map $R \to A$ is \'etale. We say that $f$ is {\it \'etale} if it is \'etale at every point of $X$. A morphism of affine schemes $f : X \to S$ is called {\it standard \'etale} if $X \to S$ is isomorphic to $$ \Spec(R[x]_h/(g)) \to \Spec(R) $$ where $R \to R[x]_h/(g)$ is a standard \'etale ring map, see Algebra, Definition \ref{algebra-definition-standard-etale}, i.e., $g$ is monic and $g'$ invertible in $R[x]_h/(g)$.

label: lemma-etale-characterize
statement: Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes. The following are equivalent The morphism $f$ is \'etale. For every affine opens $U \subset X$, $V \subset S$ with $f(U) \subset V$ the ring map $\mathcal{O}_S(V) \to \mathcal{O}_X(U)$ is \'etale. There exists an open covering $S = \bigcup_{j \in J} V_j$ and open coverings $f^{-1}(V_j) = \bigcup_{i \in I_j} U_i$ such that each of the morphisms $U_i \to V_j$, $j\in J, i\in I_j$ is \'etale. There exists an affine open covering $S = \bigcup_{j \in J} V_j$ and affine open coverings $f^{-1}(V_j) = \bigcup_{i \in I_j} U_i$ such that the ring map $\mathcal{O}_S(V_j) \to \mathcal{O}_X(U_i)$ is \'etale, for all $j\in J, i\in I_j$. Moreover, if $f$ is \'etale then for any open subschemes $U \subset X$, $V \subset S$ with $f(U) \subset V$ the restriction $f|_U : U \to V$ is \'etale.

label: lemma-composition-etale
statement: The composition of two morphisms which are \'etale is \'etale.

label: lemma-base-change-etale
statement: The base change of a morphism which is \'etale is \'etale.

label: lemma-etale-smooth-unramified
statement: Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes. Let $x \in X$. Then $f$ is \'etale at $x$ if and only if $f$ is smooth and unramified at $x$.

label: lemma-etale-locally-quasi-finite
statement: An \'etale morphism is locally quasi-finite.

label: lemma-etale-over-field
slogan: Description of the \'etale schemes over fields and fibres of \'etale morphisms.
statement: Fibres of \'etale morphisms. Let $X$ be a scheme over a field $k$. The structure morphism $X \to \Spec(k)$ is \'etale if and only if $X$ is a disjoint union of spectra of finite separable field extensions of $k$. If $f : X \to S$ is an \'etale morphism, then for every $s \in S$ the fibre $X_s$ is a disjoint union of spectra of finite separable field extensions of $\kappa(s)$.

label: lemma-etale-flat-etale-fibres
statement: Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes. If $f$ is flat, locally of finite presentation, and for every $s \in S$ the fibre $X_s$ is a disjoint union of spectra of finite separable field extensions of $\kappa(s)$, then $f$ is \'etale.

label: lemma-open-immersion-etale
statement: Any open immersion is \'etale.

label: lemma-etale-syntomic
statement: An \'etale morphism is syntomic.

label: lemma-etale-locally-finite-presentation
statement: An \'etale morphism is locally of finite presentation.

label: lemma-etale-flat
statement: An \'etale morphism is flat.

label: lemma-etale-open
statement: An \'etale morphism is open.

label: lemma-etale-locally-standard-etale
statement: Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes. Let $x \in X$ be a point. Let $V \subset S$ be an affine open neighbourhood of $f(x)$. The following are equivalent The morphism $f$ is \'etale at $x$. There exist an affine open $U \subset X$ with $x \in U$ and $f(U) \subset V$ such that the induced morphism $f|_U : U \to V$ is standard \'etale (see Definition \ref{definition-etale}).

label: lemma-etale-at-point
statement: Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes. Let $x \in X$. Set $s = f(x)$. Assume $f$ is locally of finite presentation. The following are equivalent: The morphism $f$ is \'etale at $x$. The local ring map $\mathcal{O}_{S, s} \to \mathcal{O}_{X, x}$ is flat and $X_s \to \Spec(\kappa(s))$ is \'etale at $x$. The local ring map $\mathcal{O}_{S, s} \to \mathcal{O}_{X, x}$ is flat and $X_s \to \Spec(\kappa(s))$ is unramified at $x$. The local ring map $\mathcal{O}_{S, s} \to \mathcal{O}_{X, x}$ is flat and the $\mathcal{O}_{X, x}$-module $\Omega_{X/S, x}$ is zero. The local ring map $\mathcal{O}_{S, s} \to \mathcal{O}_{X, x}$ is flat and the $\kappa(x)$-vector space $$ \Omega_{X_s/s, x} \otimes_{\mathcal{O}_{X_s, x}} \kappa(x) = \Omega_{X/S, x} \otimes_{\mathcal{O}_{X, x}} \kappa(x) $$ is zero. The local ring map $\mathcal{O}_{S, s} \to \mathcal{O}_{X, x}$ is flat, we have $\mathfrak m_s\mathcal{O}_{X, x} = \mathfrak m_x$ and the field extension $\kappa(x)/\kappa(s)$ is finite separable. There exist affine opens $U \subset X$, and $V \subset S$ such that $x \in U$, $f(U) \subset V$ and the induced morphism $f|_U : U \to V$ is standard smooth of relative dimension $0$. There exist affine opens $\Spec(A) = U \subset X$ and $\Spec(R) = V \subset S$ with $x \in U$ corresponding to $\mathfrak q \subset A$, and $f(U) \subset V$ such that there exists a presentation $$ A = R[x_1, \ldots, x_n]/(f_1, \ldots, f_n) $$ with $$ g = \det \left( \begin{matrix} \partial f_1/\partial x_1 & \partial f_2/\partial x_1 & \ldots & \partial f_n/\partial x_1 \\ \partial f_1/\partial x_2 & \partial f_2/\partial x_2 & \ldots & \partial f_n/\partial x_2 \\ \ldots & \ldots & \ldots & \ldots \\ \partial f_1/\partial x_n & \partial f_2/\partial x_n & \ldots & \partial f_n/\partial x_n \end{matrix} \right) $$ mapping to an element of $A$ not in $\mathfrak q$. There exist affine opens $U \subset X$, and $V \subset S$ such that $x \in U$, $f(U) \subset V$ and the induced morphism $f|_U : U \to V$ is standard \'etale. There exist affine opens $\Spec(A) = U \subset X$ and $\Spec(R) = V \subset S$ with $x \in U$ corresponding to $\mathfrak q \subset A$, and $f(U) \subset V$ such that there exists a presentation $$ A = R[x]_Q/(P) = R[x, 1/Q]/(P) $$ with $P, Q \in R[x]$, $P$ monic and $P' = \text{d}P/\text{d}x$ mapping to an element of $A$ not in $\mathfrak q$.

label: lemma-flat-unramified-etale
statement: A morphism is \'etale at a point if and only if it is flat and G-unramified at that point. A morphism is \'etale if and only if it is flat and G-unramified.

label: lemma-set-points-where-fibres-etale
statement: Let $$ \xymatrix{ X' \ar[r]_{g'} \ar[d]_{f'} & X \ar[d]^f \\ S' \ar[r]^g & S } $$ be a cartesian diagram of schemes. Let $W \subset X$, resp.\ $W' \subset X'$ be the open subscheme of points where $f$, resp.\ $f'$ is \'etale. Then $W' = (g')^{-1}(W)$ if $f$ is flat and locally of finite presentation, or $f$ is locally of finite presentation and $g$ is flat.

label: lemma-etale-permanence-better
statement: Let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of schemes over $S$. If $X$ is \'etale over $S$ and $Y$ is unramified over $S$, then $f$ is \'etale.

label: lemma-etale-permanence
slogan: Cancellation law for \'etale morphisms
statement: Let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of schemes over $S$. If $X$ and $Y$ are \'etale over $S$, then $f$ is \'etale.

label: lemma-etale-permanence-two
statement: Let $$ \xymatrix{ X \ar[rr]_f \ar[rd]_p & & Y \ar[dl]^q \\ & S } $$ be a commutative diagram of morphisms of schemes.
